question: The Physical Quality of Life Index does NOT include which of the following indicators?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender development index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index** does NOT include Gender development index.
 
• **The Gender Development Index (GDI) **is a metric crafted to assess gender equality. 
 
• It, along with the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM), was introduced in the 1995 Human Development Report by the United Nations Development Program. 
 
• These measures were devised to imbue the Human Development Index (HDI) with a gender-sensitive perspective. The GDI was the initial outcome of this effort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) **seeks to gauge a country's well-being by averaging three equally weighted statistics: basic literacy rate at age 15, infant mortality, and life expectancy at age one.
 
• Developed in the mid-1970s by M.D. Morris for the Overseas Development Council, emerged from dissatisfaction with using Gross National Product (GNP) alone as a development indicator.
 
• Morris aimed to capture various aspects of development, including health, education, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• While PQLI offers an improvement, it faces challenges inherent in quantifying quality of life. Critics point out the overlap between infant mortality and life expectancy as a limitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The level of physical quality **of life is often seen as indicative of a country's economic development.
 
• A country with a higher physical quality of life is typically considered more developed than one with a lower quality.
 
• This assessment is based on three key standards: the extent of education, life expectancy, and infant mortality rate.
